title: How extreme rain is putting orangutans at risk
description:
Orangutans are the world’s most endangered apes and they’re now even closer to extinction. They live on two islands in southeast Asia: Sumatra and Borneo. In November, an extreme weather event in the area killed more than 1,000 people there, plus about 7% of the world’s rarest type of orangutan according to a new study.

BBC Climate and Science reporter Georgina Rannard takes us through how orangutans are being pushed towards extinction and what some countries and charities are doing to protect them.

We also hear from a conservationist making an effort to save the species.

summaryZh: 這集談到紅毛猩猩 ( orangutan ) 的生存危機，牠們主要生活在 Sumatra 和 Borneo 的森林與低地沼澤。大規模種植棕櫚油、採礦、伐林和非法買賣等人類活動正破壞棲地，並使族群愈來愈孤立。去年十一月一次極端天氣造成大量雨量與山崩，不僅奪走逾一千人性命，也令約 7% 的 Tapanuli 紅毛猩猩死亡，顯示極端氣候會加劇滅絕風險。國際與在地保育組織透過設立受保護區、基因保育計畫與以金錢激勵保護森林等方式嘗試減緩威脅。
summaryEn: This episode explains how orangutans face growing threats. They live mainly in the rainforests and lowland swamps of Sumatra and Borneo. Large-scale palm oil plantations, mining, logging and illegal trafficking are destroying habitat and isolating groups. An extreme rainfall and landslides last November killed over 1,000 people and about 7% of the Tapanuli orangutan population, showing how extreme weather raises extinction risk. Conservation groups are protecting forest zones, running breeding and genetic programs, and promoting payments to keep forests standing.
